title.narrative: Shomotay Tarunno – youth-led advocacy for equality in Bangladesh

description.narrative: According to the Gender Inequality index, Bangladesh ranked 131i and in Global Gender Gap Report 2023￼ Bangladesh ranked 59th position. A study of Plan (2021) found that 86.8% of female respondents have faced forms of domestic violence and 26.1% avoids leaving home due to fear of violence. 90.2% girl respondents faced mental health issues due to harassment at educational institutions. ￼ As per the Legal Framework Analysis on Challenging Fear of Violence conducted by Plan (2021) several laws are outdated and require reform. Patriarchal system and deeply rooted gender stereotypes are a huge barrier towards achieving equal rights for all. Due to these stereotypes, girls and young women have less resources and access to decision-making; are not able to fund their ideas for bringing systemic change. Harmful gender stereotypes are further perpetuated by media’s framing and narratives about ‘supposed’ gender roles, the negative portrayal of GYW which are often based on outdated stereotypes, and the objectification of their bodies.Specific language is used as a means to secure patriarchal culture & gender stereotypes. Gender equitable education is often not included in curricula.

SUMMARY In Bangladesh, the existence of harmful and discriminatory gender stereotypes strengthened by various media incl. social media and government, has victimised and constricted girls and young women, and boys and men to act outside their traditional gender roles. In order to address negative stereotyping, ‘Shomotay Tarunno’ aims to enable young people in all their diversities to challenge gender stereotypes limiting them from enjoying their full potential. Plan International and JAAGO Foundation will work together to amplify the rights, representation and resources of young people, from local to national level to combat harmful gender stereotypes. By addressing the harmful gender norms throughout the life-course, building youth agency, advancing strategic partnerships with media, education and government institutions, and improving the positions of girls and young women with support of men and boys, the project will respond to the needs and rights of youth over the period of 2024-2027.

TTo achieve objective 1 ‘Young people in all their diversity are equipped to combat gender stereotypes and increase positive social gender norms in society through enhanced inclusive, effective and meaningful engagement in decision making and activism’, we will be conducting workshops, train youth trainers and implement training courses on gender rights, stereotypes, safeguarding, digital safety, media literacy and lobby and advocacy. To ensure youth will have the capacity to claim their rights and change social norms and stereotypes with their community,a perception survey will be conducted to identify the current knowledge of youth on gender stereotypes. Other important target groups are the youth-led organisations (YLOs) and the National Youth Council (NYC). The assumption is that 1) if YLOs and the NYC are capacitated on organisational development, gender equality, lobby and advocacy, media literacy, digital safety, and 2) if YLOs are provided with resources to fund their own (lobby) actions, YLOs with the support of the NYC, will be capable to influence duty bearers and the media, through their enhanced inclusive, effective and meaningful engagement in decision making and activism. The project will also support youth to use the media scorecard, Plan’s and Jaago’'s accountability tool, which will provide space to youth to monitor and report gender stereotyping messages and portrayals in local and national media and to share their findings with local and national government and media stakeholders. The accountability tool, with support of the intergenerational dialogues and advocacy workshops with duty bearers, YLOs, NYC, and consortium partners, will enable youth to hold media accountable for gender transformative messaging and gives them access to decision making spaces. With proper knowledge, information, advocacy, tools, resources, skills and space, it is anticipated that youth and YLOs will be enabled to positively change gender stereotype narratives and achieve objective 1. The project aims to work with media platforms, houses and media influentials to positively change the media narratives on gender stereotypes, which will result in Objective 2: “Media organisations, outlets and influencers are more proactive and responsive to positive gender representation and produce gender sensitive content”. To achieve this objective, the project will work with all forms of media, including social media platforms like Facebook, tiktok, youtube, instagram, which are used by most young people these days as well as with young media influencers to promote gender equality in the social media. It is presumed that if we partner with influencers and social media platforms, launch a social media campaign and build the capacity of local content creators through training and a bootcamp on how to create gender transformative content, awareness has been raised and attitudes, perceptions, and behaviours of social media influencers and local content creators have been shaped to jointly combat gender stereotypes. In the project, Strategic partnerships with different media agencies, especially print, broadcast and entertainment media will be established to promote innovative gender transformative media messaging in social and traditional media as well as to get critical insights in support of policy influencing. Based on these consultations, outputs and activities will be more specifically determined in the inception phase. Leveraging Plan International Bangladesh’s partnership with Grameen phone and Unilever, the project will initiate discussion on collaboration on gender transformative advertisements, which can reach other private entities, and millions of consumers in Bangladesh. By establishing strategic partnerships, and educating media, ownership among media professionals a conducive environment will be promoted to address gender stereotypes. The consortium aims to create sustainable impact through engaging with local and national government and education/language institutes to bring systematic change through improved legal frameworks and curricula and strengthened commitment and accountability of duty bearers, media and education institutes (Objective 3). To achieve this objective, the project is aiming to establish partnerships with Ministry of Youth and Sports, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of ICT, Ministry of Education and Ministry of Women and Children Affairs. When we have established and strengthened partnerships, we will review laws, policies and regulations on gender stereotyping in the media, identify gaps and start influencing the ministries to reduce gender bias and discrimination in relevant laws and policies. Further, the project aims to develop strategic partnerships with tertiary education and language institutes to support the revision of curricula and Bangla language and to train teachers on gender transformative education.

Target groups Youth in all their diversity of age between 15 – 24 years: 5974 (who will be reached through objective 1 and 2). The gender ratio would be 50% girls and 50% boys and 1% of total direct target group will be from youth from different gender identities and indigenous youth.
Primary duty bearers (indirect): 4000 Community stakeholders representing caregivers/parents, teachers, religious leaders, Research Institute, local government in 8 divisions, media institutes, private sector actors, 680 government and tertiary education and language institute teachers and authorities.
Secondary duty bearers (indirect): more than (>) 2 million general public is expected to reach through objective 2 (media interventions) and objective 3 on improved legal frameworks and curricula that address gender stereotyping in the media.

The potential wider impact of the project is enormous, delivering positive change at individual, community policy level and national level. Sustainability will be achieved through using the evidence and learning from the project to improve policy frameworks and curricula and to inform good practice, and to develop this model more widely in Bangladesh and beyond. By strengthening linkages and influencing the promotion of equal representation, gender rights, capacities and resources among youth, including GYW, the project focuses on the following types of sustainability: Sustained legal framework and Institutional Linkages through partnerships with several Ministries and the Youth National Council Sustained linkages will also be created with the educational sector, , including universities, teacher education institutes and higher education/ language institutes, to transform their curricula, teach teachers about our gender transformative approach and review the Bangla language ensuring a systemic change in the education sector, where young students are educated through a gender transformative approach and through gender transformative language, which they will embrace, carry out in society and continue in their future career. Sustained linkages with on- and offline media and Influencers to change the narrative in media landscape and promote a culture that embraces gender equality Sustained Capacity, representation and resources for youth organisations across 8 divisions in Bangladesh: Environmental sustainability: Project activities will be monitored to ensure that the project has no detrimental environmental impacts.

The project has identified three major dimensions through which the overall goal of the project which is “Young people, in all their diversity especially GYW, are able to live a life free of violence, voice their opinions, and resource their actions to challenge gender stereotypes” will be aimed. To achieve the goal the project will primarily work with three major stakeholders: 1) youth, youth led Organizations and the National Youth Council; 2) media organisations, outlets and media influentials and 3) the government and education institutes, including universities. The project will work in three interlinked objectives where: a) Young people in all their diversity are equipped to combat gender stereotypes and increase positive social gender norms in society through enhanced inclusive, effective and meaningful engagement in decision making and activism. b) Media organizations and outlets and influencers are more proactive and responsive to positive gender representation and produce gender sensitive content. c) Improved legal frameworks and curricula have become in place and strengthened commitment and accountability of duty bearers, media and education institutes to address harmful gender stereotypes Our strategy to achieve the objectives involves influencing power holders including media, community leaders, education institutes and duty bearers, strengthening their laws and policies, teaching skills and curricula, mobilizing young people and civil society and promoting positive attitudes, behaviors and practices from the individual, to the national and the global level. The proposed project, strategies and interventions are very much aligned with, and directly contribute to Sustainable Development Goal number 5, to end all forms of discrimination against women and girls everywhere.

The project is elaborated based on all consortium partners strategies, as it will be contributing to Plan International Bangladesh Country Strategy (2020 – 2030), Strategic Objective to ‘Empower children and young people as drivers of systemic change to gender norms and power relationships’ by youth as drivers of change and to promote and enabling environment for youth, with special attention for girls and young women. The project is also aligned with Plan International Netherlands Strategy (2021 – 2025) to stimulate youth-led lobby and advocacy, in contribution of “well-resourced feminist and youth-led organizing, activism and advocacy” and “to build youth's ability to take collective action and influence governments and duty bearers”.The strategic objective of JAAGO Foundation aligns perfectly with the objective of the project which is to "empower youth as catalysts of gender equality and inclusiveness". The strategies of the project (on e.g. youth empowerment, capacity strengthening of youth trainers, and youth-led organizations, the media and duty bearers, and to influence media organizations and platforms to produce gender-sensitive content) collectively work towards creating a more inclusive and gender equal society in line with JAAGO's Foundation's strategic objectives. By aligning with Plan International's strategies, JAAGO Foundation aims to cultivate a well-resourced and youth-led movement that empowers young people to collectively influence decision-makers and drive systemic change in societal norms and power dynamics.

recipient-country.narrative: In Bangladesh, the existence of harmful and discriminatory gender stereotypes published by various media domains incl. social media, has increased victimisation. Girls and women, as well as boys and men, are constricted by stereotypes and are socially penalized if they act outside their traditional gender roles. In order to address negative stereotyping, this project ‘Shomotay Tarunno’ aims to enable young people in all their diversities, including girls and young women, to challenge gender stereotypes that limit and stop them from enjoying their full potential. Plan International and JAAGO Foundation will work together to amplify the rights, representation and resources of young people, in all their diversity, from local to national level to combat harmful gender stereotypes. By addressing the harmful gender norms throughout the life-course, building youth agency, advancing strategic partnerships with media, education and government institutions, and improving basic conditions and positions of youth in all their diversity including girls, and young women in the family, society, and state level, while working with boys and young men to embrace gender equality and exercise positive and diverse masculinities, the project will respond to the needs and interests of youth in all their diversities, and foster an enabling environment for gender equality and girls’ rights.
